column6: I'm not allowed to tell you who made this wine.
We discounted this wine so much, we had to sign an NDA.
This wine is so discounted, the producer is anonymous.
This wine's story will make you love the deal even more.
I can tell you where it's from, though. In the thirteen hundreds the Pope moved his court to Avignon, and the vineyards just up the river became the papal wine supply.
The village is still called Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the Pope's new castle.
The vineyards look surprisingly like a dry riverbed. They're covered in galets roulés, round stones the Rhône left behind, which soak up the sun all day and keep the vines warm at night.
Every grape is picked by hand, and the growers wrote their own quality rules in the nineteen-twenties, before France even had a national system.
This one comes from a producer behind some of the region's best-known bottles. He bottled this to create a new staple of the appellation.
But they made it for us on one condition: their name stays off the front. If you want to know who it is, you'll have to buy a bottle.
It has an intense, typically Châteauneuf flavour of black fruit, spicy black pepper, wild herbs and an undertone of leather to finish.
It's a top one percent wine in the world. Jeb Dunnuck, who's spent years tasting just Rhône reds, gave it ninety-three. Jeff Leve and Vinous both have it above ninety as well.
It should be eighty pounds per bottle. On Winedrops it's just twenty.
But it's one of the region's best. This deal will end, so get it while you can.
